goalsQuestion: What publishing and reading traffic, follower distribution, latency and freshness should I use?
constraintsQuestion: What should successful publishing, retention and deletion guarantee?
requirementsAnswer: I will estimate publishing and feed reads separately using the discussed daily volumes, ten-times peak factor and follower counts, with p95 feed reads below 500 milliseconds and normal new-post visibility within 5 seconds.
coreExplanation: The publish API durably stores an immutable post ID, author ID and timestamp before acknowledging, and records fanout work; a worker looks up followers and writes post IDs to each reader's feed.
Feed reads merge ordered post IDs, filter by current follow state and visibility, and use a timestamp plus post-ID cursor so incoming posts do not shift already paginated results.
validationExplanation: For popular creators I read recent posts on demand and merge them with prepared entries, while monitoring fanout backlog, propagation delay and p95 feed latency against the 5-second and 500-millisecond goals.

If a worker fails I replay durable events idempotently; deletion writes a visibility marker checked during reads and invalidates cached entries within 60 seconds so a replay cannot resurrect the deleted post.
weakAnswer: Every post is copied synchronously to every user, whether they follow its author or not. Pagination uses a shifting offset, and a deleted post remains visible indefinitely in prepared feeds.
reviewFocus: A following-based feed must not include every creator for every user.
A shifting offset alone does not provide stable continuation under new posts.
Unbounded deleted-post visibility contradicts the 60-second requirement.
